newsitem.title: HONG KONG: After a dim start, China Everbright now dazzles.
newsitem.headline: After a dim start, China Everbright now dazzles.

text.p: After losing its glow in the 1980's, the lights are blazing again at China Everbright Holdings Co Ltd, a Beijing-backed investment vehicle in Hong Kong.

Analysts who had lost interest in a tangled, unfocused business are now paying attention, searching for signs of how China intends to match its political clout with economic muscle in Hong Kong after it takes over the British colony in 11 days.
So far, the signs have been written in neon.
Last month, China Everbright bought a major stake in Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd, the jewel in the crown of Britain's Cable and Wireless Ltd Plc.
Then a Hong Kong-listed unit acquired a stake in a mainland Chinese bank, offering foreign investors a rare play on the tightly guarded domestic Chinese banking industry.
But while these flashy moves dazzled, investors are blinking in the glare, trying to see the logic behind the acquisitions and harder still to work out Everbright's next move.
Nonetheless, shares in China Everbright-IHD Pacific Ltd HK, the group's flagship in Hong Kong, have rocketed by more than 600 percent in the first six months of this year.
"In terms of potential, China Everbright is definitely the favoured vehicle of the State Council," said a Hong Kong analyst familiar with the group, referring to the Chinese cabinet.

China Everbright Group, along with China International Trust and Investment Corp (CITIC), were set up in the early 1980's in the first flush of China's "Open Door" reform policies pioneered by the late paramount leader Deng Xiaoping.
Although they had ministry-level status and reported directly to the State Council, the shine quickly wore off Everbright as it grew large and unwieldy.
Everbright subsidiaries made everything from telephones to timber products, launched into banking and real estate and dabbled in insurance.

The Hong Kong holding company has three listed units in Hong Kong, Everbright-IHD, China Everbright Technology Ltd and China Everbright International Ltd. In Singapore, the group is represented by HTP Holdings Ltd.
But the new man who took over Everbright group's helm last year quickly changed investor perceptions.
Zhu Xiaohua, 48, a former vice governor of China's central bank, is a protege of Beijing's economic supremo, Zhu Rongji. Urbane and knowledgeable, he is well liked by foreign businessmen.
"I believe my experience as an administrator of the central bank gives me a better understanding of the economy -- a clearer picture than others," Zhu told Hong Kong's Capital magazine.
"You could say risk management is my main business."
"The Everbright group is mainly finance and investment management and my previous experience helps me here," Zhu said.
Investors and analysts had expected Zhu's appointment to sharpen the group's focus on finance.
So when the Hong Kong holding company said it bought a 7.74 percent stake in Hongkong Telecom Ltd from CITIC's Hong Kong arm, CITIC Pacific Ltd, it was a complete surprise.
"Anything can happen with China Everbright nowadays," said one Hong Kong broker.

Market focus has been on 57 percent-held Everbright-IHD, the group's banking and finance arm. Last week, Chinese authorities approved its acquisition of a 20 percent stake in Everbright Bank of China.
Everbright-IHD shares closed on Friday at HK$19.40 against HK$2.70 at end December 1996, an increase of 619 percent.
What has excited investors is the prospect of ground floor entry to commercial banking in China.
"The concept has novelty value but the premium is a bit steep for a sector that will remain under tight government control," the Hong Kong analyst said.
